statement:
A geometric point of a scheme is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with algebraically closed $\Omega$; its étale stalk is a filtered colimit over pointed étale neighborhoods. A *strictly henselian local ring* is henselian with separably closed residue field. $H^q_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)$ means right-derived global sections of an **abelian sheaf** $\mathcal F$ on the small étale site; ordinary global sections $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ also make sense for sheaves of sets. For a ring $R$, “every local ring of $R$ is strictly henselian” means this for $R_\mathfrak p$ at each prime. An integral normal scheme has a function field at its generic point; the function field is *separably closed* if it has no nontrivial separable finite extensions. For $f\in R$, $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$.

**Standalone theorem (source data preserved):**
Let $S$ be a scheme all of whose local rings are strictly henselian.
Then for any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $S_\etale$ we have
$H^i(S_\etale, \mathcal{F}) = H^i(S_{Zar}, \mathcal{F})$.

**Scope and typing:** All original assumptions and the precise sheaf/site categories have been retained; all source abbreviations use the definitions above.

statement:
A geometric point of a scheme is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with algebraically closed $\Omega$; its étale stalk is a filtered colimit over pointed étale neighborhoods. A *strictly henselian local ring* is henselian with separably closed residue field. $H^q_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)$ means right-derived global sections of an **abelian sheaf** $\mathcal F$ on the small étale site; ordinary global sections $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ also make sense for sheaves of sets. An integral normal scheme has a function field at its generic point; the function field is *separably closed* if it has no nontrivial separable finite extensions. **Standalone theorem (source data preserved):**
Let $X$ be an affine scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists an integral surjective morphism $X' \to X$ such that for
every closed subscheme $Z' \subset X'$, every finite abelian group $M$, and
every $q \geq 1$ we have $H^q_\etale(Z', \underline{M}) = 0$.
\item For any closed subscheme $Z \subset X$, finite abelian group $M$,
$q \geq 1$, and $\xi \in H^q_\etale(Z, \underline{M})$ there exists a
finite surjective morphism $X' \to X$ of finite presentation such that
$\xi$ pulls back to zero in $H^q_\etale(X' \times_X Z, \underline{M})$.
\end{enumerate}
